page: OVHcloud c3-128 is a compute-optimized virtual instance built on AMD EPYC x86_64 processors running under the KVM hypervisor. The instance is configured with 64 dedicated physical cores (64 vCPUs) running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz, with one thread per core (simultaneous multithreading is disabled). It provides 128 GB of system memory, matching a 1:2 compute-optimized ratio of 2.0 GB RAM per core. The package includes 400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, an 8 Gbps baseline network interface, and no attached GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-threaded computational and memory throughput. The instance ranks in the top 10% on multi-core stress-ng tests, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, PassMark CPU scores, and software compilation via Clang. It also registers top-tier results in Redis SET operations (137.31 million ops/sec) and cached memory bandwidth. In contrast, single-threaded metrics reflect the 2.3 GHz clock frequency, registering average tier performance in single-core Geekbench and single-threaded gzip and bzip3 tasks. Additionally, the CPU does not support AVX-512 extensions.

OVHcloud c3-128 offers high core-density economics for highly parallel processing pipelines. The inclusion of 400 GB NVMe local storage facilitates low-latency temporary data operations without requiring secondary volume attachments. However, users running single-threaded bottlenecks, large-scale vector acceleration requiring AVX-512, or memory-heavy applications requiring high RAM ratios may experience architectural limits.

This server is suited for CPU-bound multi-threaded workloads, including software compilation farms, continuous integration and deployment (CI/CD) pipelines, batch data processing, physics simulations, and high-throughput in-memory caching nodes.
